The beginner guidance flow: ask, describe, insert, repair
Favicon Icon Design: badge, glyph and brand colour forming one mark
Favicon Design Constraints: vector delivery, tab-size legibility, static asset path

nodes.label: The beginner's question: what am I allowed to put here?
nodes.rationale: Existing XML editors answer 'is this valid?', an expert's question that is only useful once you already know what the document should look like. Validators are yes/no oracles over complete documents, so a guidance engine has to be built rather than layered on.
nodes.norm_label: the beginner's question: what am i allowed to put here?

nodes.label: Static client-only SPA, documents never leave the browser
nodes.rationale: No server means the privacy promise is enforceable rather than merely stated; deploys to GitHub Pages from main.
nodes.norm_label: static client-only spa, documents never leave the browser
nodes.community_name: Security model: client-side is not a security property

nodes.label: Lossless round-tripping (what works today)
nodes.community_name: Lossless CST document model, not the DOM

nodes.label: Product thesis: guidance is the product, not a layer over a validator
nodes.rationale: No validator exposes the content-model state machine needed to answer position-sensitive questions mid-edit. A team that treats guidance as a thin layer over a validator discovers in month five that it cannot be built that way and ships an expert tool by accident.
nodes.norm_label: product thesis: guidance is the product, not a layer over a validator

nodes.label: Stated non-goals: phones, collaboration, text editor, server
nodes.rationale: Stated explicitly so they are decisions rather than omissions.
nodes.norm_label: stated non-goals: phones, collaboration, text editor, server

nodes.label: Verification status audit trail
nodes.rationale: Research agents had no network access, so their package claims were model recall; everything load-bearing was re-verified against primary sources and anything unverified is a spike rather than a decision.

nodes.label: Stack: boring choices, novelty budget spent on the schema engine
nodes.rationale: React 19 for ecosystem depth in virtualized tree/overlays/command palette; Vite for module-worker and WASM handling; CodeMirror 6 over Monaco at ~10x smaller; rejected Next.js, Redux Toolkit, MUI/Mantine, react-arborist.
nodes.norm_label: stack: boring choices, novelty budget spent on the schema engine

nodes.label: Lossless CST document model, not the DOM
nodes.rationale: The browser DOM destroys data silently — expands entity references, drops the DOCTYPE internal subset, never emits the XML declaration, rewrites to , normalises attribute quoting, invents namespace prefixes. Users keep these files in git and a reformat-on-save produces a 4,000-line diff and gets the tool banned.
nodes.norm_label: lossless cst document model, not the dom
nodes.community_name: Lossless CST document model, not the DOM

nodes.label: Splice serializer: slice clean subtrees verbatim
nodes.rationale: Makes byte-exact round-tripping structural rather than a matter of getting a hundred formatting details right, and makes serialisation O(changed) rather than O(document).
nodes.norm_label: splice serializer: slice clean subtrees verbatim
nodes.community_name: Lossless CST document model, not the DOM

nodes.label: Labelled command log with inverses
nodes.rationale: Human-readable labels generated at construction time are what make a visible History panel possible; quick fixes return commands too, so a fix is atomically undoable as one step. Undo always moves focus and scrolls to the affected node — silent undo is the top complaint about prior art.
nodes.community_name: Lossless CST document model, not the DOM

nodes.label: State split: command log, Zustand, XState
nodes.rationale: XState used narrowly for exactly three flows where boolean-flag soup would otherwise emerge — the wizard, drag-and-drop, and the validation lifecycle. Stable NodeIds mean selection, expansion and validation results survive edits.
nodes.norm_label: state split: command log, zustand, xstate
nodes.community_name: Lossless CST document model, not the DOM

nodes.label: Hand-rolled typed worker protocol
nodes.rationale: Rather than Comlink: revision tagging and terminate-and-respawn cancellation are exactly what Comlink's transparent-proxy model hides. Stale results render dimmed rather than cleared so the UI never flickers to 'no problems' mid-edit.

nodes.label: XSD 1.1 in scope, our engine is the primary verdict
nodes.rationale: No JavaScript XSD 1.1 validator exists; libxml2 is 1.0-only and its maintainer says 1.1 is not planned. The saving grace is that the schema engine was always being written anyway, and the two headline 1.1 features are XPath-shaped so fontoxpath (already mandatory for Schematron) makes assertions cheap.
nodes.norm_label: xsd 1.1 in scope, our engine is the primary verdict

nodes.label: libxml2-wasm as the fast XSD 1.0 differential oracle
nodes.norm_label: libxml2-wasm as the fast xsd 1.0 differential oracle

nodes.label: xmlschema under Pyodide as the authoritative XSD 1.1 oracle
nodes.rationale: Pure Python with only elementpath as a dependency, so micropip installs it under Pyodide with no C extensions to cross-compile. Heavy (~6-10MB) so it loads lazily in its own worker behind an explicit user action; in CI it runs under plain CPython and costs nothing.
nodes.norm_label: xmlschema under pyodide as the authoritative xsd 1.1 oracle

nodes.label: Differential harness dispatches on the schema's declared version
nodes.rationale: A 1.1-legal schema can be UPA-invalid under 1.0, so a 1.0 oracle pointed at a 1.1 schema drowns the harness in false failures. Version dispatch does not trust vc:minVersion — a schema using 1.1 constructs is 1.1 whether or not it says so.
nodes.norm_label: differential harness dispatches on the schema's declared version

nodes.label: Direct Schematron interpreter over fontoxpath, not XSLT
nodes.rationale: Better on four axes: no XSLT engine to break in November 2026; fontoxpath is a mandatory dependency regardless so the marginal cost is one module; findings bind to nodes by identity rather than an SVRL @location string; per-rule statistics become possible. Written from scratch rather than forked from node-schematron because the reusable parts are the ones our CST and XPath facade already provide.
nodes.norm_label: direct schematron interpreter over fontoxpath, not xslt
nodes.community_name: whatCanGoHere: forward run intersected with backward co-reachability

nodes.label: Chrome removes XSLT in v158 (17 Nov 2026)
nodes.rationale: Any design depending on the browser's XSLTProcessor has a hard expiry date; Firefox and WebKit have signalled they will follow. The alternative runtime SaxonJS 2 is free of charge but proprietary, an easy trap since 'free' reads as 'open source'.
nodes.norm_label: chrome removes xslt in v158 (17 nov 2026)
nodes.community_name: whatCanGoHere: forward run intersected with backward co-reachability

nodes.label: Error to node mapping: own the serializer, return a lineMap
nodes.rationale: Emit exactly one element start-tag per line when serialising for validation so libxml2's 'line 42' is an O(1) array lookup, and column numbers — which libxml2 reports as 0 for schema errors — become irrelevant.
nodes.norm_label: error to node mapping: own the serializer, return a linemap
nodes.community_name: Lossless CST document model, not the DOM

nodes.label: Risk 1: guidance/verdict drift
nodes.rationale: The guidance engine and libxml2 are two independent implementations of XSD semantics; disagreement means the product actively teaches beginners wrong things, which destroys the value proposition. Mitigated structurally by differential CI from Phase 3 day one and a published pass rate.

nodes.label: Risk 4: bundle weight and the entry-chunk regression
nodes.rationale: A stray top-level import pulling a validator into the main chunk is a one-line mistake that costs every user the download and looks like nothing. It has already happened once — XSD 1.1 assertions statically imported fontoxpath and put 330KB into the entry chunk — so it is checked mechanically rather than remembered.
nodes.norm_label: risk 4: bundle weight and the entry-chunk regression

nodes.label: Risk 6: memory, not CPU, is the ceiling
nodes.rationale: A 50MB instance expands to 400-600MB inside the wasm32 heap and browsers OOM well below the 4GB limit; mitigation is a stated threshold policy with graceful degradation, not 'we'll optimise later'.
nodes.norm_label: risk 6: memory, not cpu, is the ceiling

nodes.label: Risk 7: File System Access API is Chromium-only
nodes.rationale: ~28% of users get save-in-place and Firefox calls it 'harmful', so the download/upload path is designed as primary with FSA as progressive enhancement, not the reverse. OPFS for autosave works everywhere.
nodes.norm_label: risk 7: file system access api is chromium-only
nodes.community_name: Security model: client-side is not a security property

nodes.label: Three-file workspace: one slot per kind (xml, xsd, sch)
nodes.rationale: An earlier design had attach-a-schema, edit-a-schema and attach-a-sample as three separate mechanisms and could not express cross-file errors; it also had a silent hole where Schematron rules were parsed from whichever document was being edited, so the bundled failing-rule example opened green. A test calling runSchematron directly could not see it.
nodes.norm_label: three-file workspace: one slot per kind (xml, xsd, sch)

nodes.label: A file is filed by its root element, not its extension
nodes.rationale: The extension is a claim; the root element is a fact, and somebody handed rules.xml should not have to rename it before the editor will run it.
nodes.norm_label: a file is filed by its root element, not its extension

nodes.label: Findings are attributed to the file they belong in
nodes.rationale: A failing assert belongs to the XML; a rule whose XPath does not evaluate belongs to the .sch; a dangling type= belongs to the XSD even though it is noticed in the XML. Filing a rule error against the XML would send someone editing a document they have not broken.
nodes.norm_label: findings are attributed to the file they belong in

nodes.label: Downstream re-derivation tiered by cost
nodes.rationale: The guidance engine recompiles in-process and synchronously so schema edits show up immediately; libxml2's schema is debounced at 500ms because setSchema terminates and respawns the worker; Schematron rules are guarded on their serialized source so typing in the XML does not reparse the .sch.

nodes.label: The Insert palette
nodes.rationale: The most important screen in the product; insertion is rendered three ways at once (ghost row, toolbar button, four key bindings) so it cannot be missed.
nodes.community_name: whatCanGoHere: forward run intersected with backward co-reachability

nodes.label: The Inspector is the selection inspector
nodes.rationale: Everything about the selected node in one fixed place is the property beginners rely on most; sections come from a per-document-kind registry so XSD and Schematron swap sections in without a second layout. Read-only projections go on the left, deliberately away from the controls that change the document.
nodes.norm_label: the inspector is the selection inspector
nodes.community_name: Inspector section stack and per-document-kind registry

nodes.label: The teaching promise cannot depend on authored documentation
nodes.rationale: Most schemas a beginner meets have no annotations at all, so describe.ts always returns a sentence generated from the compiled model. Generated descriptions are marked auto so users learn to distinguish authored guidance from inferred.
nodes.norm_label: the teaching promise cannot depend on authored documentation
nodes.community_name: whatCanGoHere: forward run intersected with backward co-reachability

nodes.label: Expert mode removes chrome, never capability
nodes.rationale: Ship the toggle on day one and make every UI decision answer 'which side of the toggle?', or beginner scaffolding accretes until the tool is slow for everyone.
nodes.norm_label: expert mode removes chrome, never capability

nodes.label: One model, three projections — never a second editable model
nodes.rationale: The XSD component tree and the Schematron semantic tree are derived projections over the same CST; every sync bug in this class of tool lives in the gap between two representations of one document.
nodes.norm_label: one model, three projections — never a second editable model

nodes.label: A schema is a graph written as a tree
nodes.rationale: type="Address" is a reference the outline cannot draw, which is why every XSD refactoring exists — each one means 'find all the edges yourself and get none of them wrong'.
nodes.norm_label: a schema is a graph written as a tree

nodes.label: Refactorings find references syntactically, not from the compiled model
nodes.rationale: Renaming has to work on a schema that does not currently compile, which is the state a schema is in for most of the time anyone is editing it. References come from a table of the twelve QName-valued attributes kept in their six symbol spaces, because ref means three different things depending on the element it sits on.
nodes.norm_label: refactorings find references syntactically, not from the compiled model

nodes.label: Three things the refactorings refuse to do
nodes.rationale: Inline a shared type, extract under a taken name, and extract when no correct reference text exists — because the alternative in each case is a confident wrong answer. A round-trip test asserts extract-then-inline returns the file byte-for-byte.
nodes.norm_label: three things the refactorings refuse to do

nodes.label: A generated document is valid and meaningless
nodes.rationale: The failure mode of every document generator, invisible without help: the badge reads green while every date says 2026-01-01. So the scaffolder marks every invented value, F7 steps through them, and fixed/default values are not marked because the schema author already decided those.
nodes.norm_label: a generated document is valid and meaningless

nodes.label: Placeholder review state is derived, not tracked
nodes.rationale: Comparing against the document is exact, costs one pass, and gets undo right for free; an intercept-the-edit scheme silently loses entries, and a test pins that case.
nodes.norm_label: placeholder review state is derived, not tracked

nodes.label: Smart paste asks before the edit
nodes.rationale: Each option's cost is measured and ranked by consequence then proximity; plain Ctrl+V goes straight through when exactly one option is valid, because turning an expert's paste into a dialogue is its own failure. The fragment is reconstructed node by node rather than regenerated from the schema, after an earlier version produced correct elements containing none of the clipboard.
nodes.norm_label: smart paste asks before the edit
nodes.community_name: whatCanGoHere: forward run intersected with backward co-reachability

nodes.label: Schema inference: permissive where evidence is thin
nodes.rationale: Anything seen twice is written unbounded because permitting one more than the file showed is a smaller mistake than rejecting the next file; every value stays xs:string because guessing xs:date from one date-shaped string rejects documents the author would have accepted. Framed as a draft with per-decision evidence, never as authoritative.
nodes.norm_label: schema inference: permissive where evidence is thin

nodes.label: Three bundled examples, one lesson each
nodes.rationale: Purchase order teaches the core loop; the topic teaches prefixes and mixed content across two namespaces and an import; the invoice is structurally perfect and wrong (total 120.00 against lines summing to 140.00). A test asserts it fails exactly one rule and goes green when corrected, so CI catches a broken first-minute demo rather than a user.
nodes.norm_label: three bundled examples, one lesson each

nodes.label: A mixed element is one tree row carrying its flow
nodes.rationale: SPIKE-4 asked the wrong question: both candidates were editors and the unusable part was the display. Marked-up runs show as angle-bracket ellipses rather than being stripped, so it is never a surprise that half a sentence is tagged, and the children stay reachable. ProseMirror was declined for ~150KB in the entry chunk plus a second document model.
nodes.norm_label: a mixed element is one tree row carrying its flow

nodes.label: FlowEditor seam (flowSource / setFlow)
nodes.rationale: The whole interface between the flow and the document, so a WYSIWYG surface can replace it later without anything else moving.

nodes.label: Table view for repeated siblings
nodes.rationale: Reading down a column is the question a tree makes hard and a grid makes free. Columns accumulate across rows so one row missing an optional child does not lose the column, and an absent cell's element is created on first edit. Nested children never become columns because their meaning would differ by depth.

nodes.label: Hand-written offline service worker
nodes.rationale: Part of the security story rather than a nicety — the premise is that documents never leave the browser, and a validator that stops working on a train contradicts its own claim. Hand-written rather than vite-plugin-pwa because the requirement is 'cache these seven files' and a dependency whose configuration surface exceeds the thing it configures is a liability. The cache name carries a content hash so a new build invalidates the old cache wholesale.
nodes.community_name: Security model: client-side is not a security property

nodes.label: First-run coach marks, never modal
nodes.rationale: Everything underneath stays clickable so someone who would rather just start is never blocked by the explanation of how to start; Escape dismisses all of them, because a person pressing Escape is telling you they do not want the tour.

nodes.label: i18n deliberately deferred
nodes.rationale: Every user-facing string is written to be read, and threading them through a message catalogue is a refactor that should happen when there is a second locale to test against, not before.
nodes.community_name: whatCanGoHere: forward run intersected with backward co-reachability

nodes.label: xs:openContent never reaches the automaton
nodes.rationale: Interleaving the whole model with a wildcard loop is a state explosion, when the same semantics fall out of removing the wildcard-matched children before the model runs.

nodes.label: Security model: client-side is not a security property
nodes.norm_label: security model: client-side is not a security property
nodes.community_name: Security model: client-side is not a security property

nodes.label: Open decisions: DTD/RELAX NG support, document size
nodes.rationale: 50MB+ files change the architecture (streaming, partial loading) rather than just the tuning; opening a DTD- or RELAX NG-based document should at minimum give a clear 'not supported'.
nodes.norm_label: open decisions: dtd/relax ng support, document size
nodes.community_name: Lossless CST document model, not the DOM

nodes.label: Survey: no library exposes an XSD component model
nodes.rationale: libxml2 keeps particles in private headers so binding harder does not help; code generators discard sequence ordering, occurrence bounds, choice structure and substitution groups, and JSON Schema cannot express xs:sequence ordering at all; real component models (Xerces2-J XSModel, Saxon-EE) are Java/.NET and would mean multi-megabyte payloads.
nodes.norm_label: survey: no library exposes an xsd component model

nodes.label: Xerces XSCMValidator.whatCanGoHere precedent
nodes.rationale: Xerces2-J's three-way split (XSDFACM, XSAllCM, XSEmptyCM) shows the approach is standard rather than invented; Xerces is Apache-2.0 so reading it is legally clean, but reimplement from the published algorithms rather than transliterating.
nodes.community_name: whatCanGoHere: forward run intersected with backward co-reachability

nodes.label: Glushkov position automaton
nodes.rationale: For 1-unambiguous expressions the Glushkov automaton is already deterministic — no subset construction, no NFA state sets, runtime state is a single integer plus a small counter vector. UPA therefore collapses the implementation cost and makes the forward run O(n).

nodes.label: Unique Particle Attribution and graceful UPA degradation
nodes.rationale: Real schemas violate UPA, including hand-written ones a beginner will bring. Detect at compile time, surface as a schema warning, and degrade the runtime to NFA state sets — refusing to open a slightly-broken schema is a product failure for our user.
nodes.norm_label: unique particle attribution and graceful upa degradation

nodes.label: whatCanGoHere: forward run intersected with backward co-reachability
nodes.rationale: The backward sweep is what makes the query genuinely position-aware rather than merely 'children allowed by this type': a suggestion is only offered if the material already present after the caret can still be completed.
nodes.norm_label: whatcangohere: forward run intersected with backward co-reachability
nodes.community_name: whatCanGoHere: forward run intersected with backward co-reachability

nodes.label: Single backward co-reachability sweep for every gap
nodes.rationale: One sweep from n down to 0 yields CoReach_i for every i simultaneously, so all insertion gaps in a parent cost O(n*|states|) together rather than per gap. Memoised on (contentModelId, hash(childNameSequence)).
nodes.norm_label: single backward co-reachability sweep for every gap

nodes.label: Numeric occurrence: unbounded / unroll / counting hybrid
nodes.rationale: Unrolling finite bounds is exactly correct and trivially debuggable but blows up, so it is gated on a ~2,000 total-position budget with a counting automaton above it. In real schemas maxOccurs is essentially always 1 or unbounded, so instrument the budget rather than assuming.
nodes.norm_label: numeric occurrence: unbounded / unroll / counting hybrid

nodes.label: AllContentModel: xs:all is a bitset, not an automaton
nodes.rationale: XSD 1.0 restricts xs:all so heavily that a seen-members bitset is simpler and faster than the automaton path, mirroring Xerces's XSAllCM. XSD 1.1 relaxes all of it, so the bitset generalises to a counter vector behind a version flag sharing the same interface.
nodes.norm_label: allcontentmodel: xs:all is a bitset, not an automaton
nodes.community_name: whatCanGoHere: forward run intersected with backward co-reachability

nodes.label: Substitution groups as symbol matchers, never expansion
nodes.rationale: On UBL or GML a head can have hundreds of members: expansion explodes the position count and destroys the 1-unambiguity that gave you a DFA. Keep one position per particle carrying matchesElement(qname).
nodes.norm_label: substitution groups as symbol matchers, never expansion

nodes.label: Effective content models (extension, restriction, xsi:type)
nodes.rationale: Restriction-legality checking is where most homegrown XSD implementations stall, and it affects schema authoring correctness rather than instance editing — so v1 skips it and routes it to a later schema-lint mode. xsi:type gets a first-class Type dropdown because 'is this a Domestic or an International address?' is exactly the question a beginner needs asked of them.

nodes.label: Wildcards: processContents drives the UI directly
nodes.rationale: strict gives a picker of global elements, lax adds a custom-name escape, skip gives a free-text box with a 'not checked' badge. Wildcard suggestions must rank below named elements in a separate section or a beginner drowns in noise.
nodes.norm_label: wildcards: processcontents drives the ui directly
nodes.community_name: whatCanGoHere: forward run intersected with backward co-reachability

nodes.label: Required-and-missing as a shortest-path BFS
nodes.rationale: BFS from the final state to the nearest accepting state, preferring concrete declarations over wildcards, yields the literal ordered list powering 'Add all 3 missing children'. mandatoryAt(i) is sound and cheap by re-testing completion with each candidate removed from the alphabet.

nodes.label: Tri-state validity badging (red / amber / green)
nodes.rationale: Falls straight out of the automaton with no extra machinery: red when the forward run dies, amber when it survives but is non-accepting, green when accepting and all value checks pass.

nodes.label: Quick fixes from error-tolerant alignment
nodes.rationale: When the prefix already fails is precisely the moment a beginner needs the most help, so do not emit 'invalid content'. Each edit operation maps one-to-one onto a quick fix (substitution to rename, deletion to remove, insertion to add, transposition to swap). Build the one algorithm deliberately rather than accreting per-error heuristics.

nodes.label: buildSkeleton and placeholder provenance
nodes.rationale: Every auto-filled value carries unfilled: true so the UI shows amber 'needs your input' rather than a green tick. Silently generating a document full of plausible fake data that validates is the worst possible outcome for a beginner — it teaches them the tool's approval is meaningless. Guarded by a type-recurrence stack, a ~500 node budget and a depth cap.

nodes.label: widgetFor(simpleTypeDef) decision table
nodes.rationale: Written as an explicit table rather than a heuristic because this is where the beginner actually spends their time.

nodes.label: XSD regex is not JavaScript regex (types/xsdRegex.ts)
nodes.rationale: XSD patterns are implicitly anchored, support character-class subtraction which JS lacks entirely, carry the \i \I \c \C XML-name escapes, and lack backreferences and lazy quantifiers. Treating them as interchangeable silently corrupts validation. Paired with a deterministic string generator over the same AST because the example is worth more to a beginner than the pattern.
nodes.norm_label: xsd regex is not javascript regex (types/xsdregex.ts)

nodes.label: describeParticle / describeType — the guaranteed fallback
nodes.rationale: Most schemas a beginner meets have no documentation at all, so synthesising plain English from the components themselves does more for the beginner experience than all the annotation plumbing combined. Annotation content is mixed and frequently contains embedded XHTML, so render as sanitised HTML rather than flattened text.
nodes.community_name: whatCanGoHere: forward run intersected with backward co-reachability

nodes.label: Pluggable xs:appinfo interpreter registry
nodes.rationale: Real-world enterprise schemas routinely encode presentation metadata in appinfo, and this is the escape hatch that makes them look good.
nodes.community_name: whatCanGoHere: forward run intersected with backward co-reachability

nodes.label: Diagnostic interface
nodes.rationale: Produce diagnostics structurally and never parse validator message strings; plain English is rendered from structured params with the spec-ese kept behind 'show details'.

nodes.label: QuickFix interface
nodes.rationale: apply() returns a Command so fixes are atomically undoable; the interface is designed now so SQF operations map onto it cleanly rather than needing a parallel mechanism later.

nodes.label: Badge roll-up and incremental revalidation
nodes.rationale: A problem here (solid dot) is rendered distinguishably from a problem inside (ring) so the user can drill down from the root; revalidation is debounced at ~150ms and incremental, with document-global constraints run in the worker on idle.

nodes.label: Error taxonomy — 20 classes, each with a plain-English rewrite and a fix
nodes.norm_label: error taxonomy — 20 classes, each with a plain-english rewrite and a fix

nodes.label: Schematron Quick Fixes (SQF)
nodes.rationale: Lets schema authors ship domain-specific one-click fixes with their rules, which no browser-based editor currently offers and which fits the teach-the-beginner thesis exactly. Scoped as a stretch item.

nodes.label: Schema-less mode: infer, but never disguise a guess as a rule
nodes.rationale: Every hint carries source: 'schema' | 'inferred' | 'heuristic' and the UI labels inferred suggestions 'learned from your document', never 'required'. A beginner must always be able to tell a rule from a guess.
nodes.norm_label: schema-less mode: infer, but never disguise a guess as a rule

nodes.label: SOA to SORE content-model inference
nodes.rationale: Roughly 300 LOC, essentially what Trang does; the same machinery powers 'Generate an XSD from this document' and from N documents.

nodes.label: Guidance degrades; the tool never does
nodes.rationale: Every editing operation stays available on an unschema'd node; four partial-schema situations get four distinct badges, including a search of ancestors and siblings for a parent whose content model does accept a rejected element.
nodes.norm_label: guidance degrades; the tool never does

nodes.label: Namespace mismatch deserves its own diagnostic
nodes.rationale: By far the most common way a beginner's document fails, and the raw validator reports an unhelpful 'no declaration found'. Detect it before generic undeclared-element handling by testing whether the local name matches a declaration in some other namespace. elementFormDefault="unqualified" is the classic trap and looks like a bug in the tool.
nodes.norm_label: namespace mismatch deserves its own diagnostic

nodes.label: OASIS XML Catalogs for resolution
nodes.rationale: So the app works offline, behind corporate firewalls, and without fetching arbitrary URLs at load time.
nodes.community_name: Security model: client-side is not a security property

nodes.label: Scope and sequencing (P1-P10), simple-type compiler is the sleeper
nodes.rationale: A pragmatic v1 dropping identity constraints, restriction-legality checking and the rarer facets lands near 3,500 LOC. Sequence P6 (particle to automaton) and P9 (query API) early — they are the product.
nodes.norm_label: scope and sequencing (p1-p10), simple-type compiler is the sleeper

nodes.label: Lazy per-type content-model compilation and IndexedDB persistence
nodes.rationale: UBL is ~2MB across many files with thousands of type definitions, so compiling everything at load is wasted work; compiled models persist keyed by a hash of the concatenated sources so reopening is instant and offline.
nodes.norm_label: lazy per-type content-model compilation and indexeddb persistence

nodes.label: Instrument compile time, position counts, unroll-budget hits, UPA violations
nodes.rationale: Those four metrics tell you whether the design assumptions survive contact with real schemas.
nodes.norm_label: instrument compile time, position counts, unroll-budget hits, upa violations

nodes.label: Kilpeläinen & Tuhkanen, regular expressions with numeric occurrence
nodes.author: Kilpeläinen, Tuhkanen
nodes.norm_label: kilpelainen & tuhkanen, regular expressions with numeric occurrence

nodes.label: Gelade, Gyssens & Martens, regular expressions with counting
nodes.author: Gelade, Gyssens, Martens
nodes.norm_label: gelade, gyssens & martens, regular expressions with counting

nodes.label: Bex, Neven & Vansummeren, Inferring XML Schema Definitions from XML Data (VLDB 2007)
nodes.author: Bex, Neven, Vansummeren
nodes.norm_label: bex, neven & vansummeren, inferring xml schema definitions from xml data (vldb 2007)

nodes.label: SPIKE-0 — no library exposes an XSD component model
nodes.rationale: Resolved by survey rather than experiment. A positive answer would have removed roughly 40% of the engineering budget. The consequence is the whole product thesis: 'what may I put here?' is not a validation feature, because no validator exposes the state machine that answers it.
nodes.norm_label: spike-0 — no library exposes an xsd component model

nodes.label: SPIKE-1 — libxml2-wasm reports all errors, with line numbers; columns are always 0
nodes.rationale: Measured against libxml2-wasm@0.7.1 with five faults in five sibling subtrees. Confirms the lineMap design and removes the need for xmllint-wasm. A structural failure truncates the rest of that element, so the Problems panel must not promise to be exhaustive after the first structural error in a subtree.
nodes.norm_label: spike-1 — libxml2-wasm reports all errors, with line numbers; columns are always 0
nodes.community_name: Lossless CST document model, not the DOM

nodes.label: SPIKE-2 — multi-file schema sets work through a registered input provider
nodes.rationale: xmlRegisterInputProvider resolves both import and include, so no flattening is needed and the fallback the plan had budgeted for is unnecessary. The provider is also the security boundary: match and open only answer for keys already in the catalogue, so there is no code path from a hostile schemaLocation to the network.
nodes.norm_label: spike-2 — multi-file schema sets work through a registered input provider
nodes.community_name: Security model: client-side is not a security property

nodes.label: SPIKE-3 — Glushkov automaton latency, partially answered
nodes.rationale: Sub-millisecond on every schema in the test suite, but the UBL 2.1 / GML 3.2 criterion waits on the corpus. The position budget marks a model approximate rather than pretending to be exact. insertionPlan deliberately does not share the single-sweep optimisation and is quadratic in child count, which is fine for one element's palette and is why it is not used to paint the tree.
nodes.norm_label: spike-3 — glushkov automaton latency, partially answered

nodes.label: SPIKE-4 — mixed content: neither candidate, and the spike asked the wrong question
nodes.rationale: Both candidate answers were editors, but the unusable part was never the editing — it was the display. Five rows is unreadable before anyone types anything, so the change that mattered is that a mixed element is one tree row carrying its flow.
nodes.norm_label: spike-4 — mixed content: neither candidate, and the spike asked the wrong question

nodes.label: Scoped source snippet flow editor
nodes.rationale: Inner XML in a textarea with the schema's permitted inline elements as wrap buttons, and nothing committed until it parses. Refusing a broken commit matters more here than anywhere else, because the alternative is discarding a paragraph someone was midway through typing.

nodes.label: ProseMirror declined
nodes.rationale: ~150 KB in the entry chunk plus a second document model to keep in step with the CST — the exact two-representations problem this codebase is arranged around, bought for a minority of documents. Risk 4 has already fired once in this project for less. What is given up is WYSIWYG.

nodes.label: libxml2-wasm needs an ES-module worker (worker: { format: 'es' })
nodes.rationale: libxml2-wasm initialises with a top-level await, which Vite's default iife worker output cannot express. The failure is a build error rather than a runtime one so it cannot reach production, but it costs an afternoon if met without warning.
nodes.norm_label: libxml2-wasm needs an es-module worker (worker: { format: 'es' })

nodes.label: Differential harness finding: abstract substitution-group head accepted
nodes.rationale: The palette already excluded abstract candidates from insertion but the validation path did not, so the engine would have called a document valid that libxml2 rejects. The fix pushes abstract down onto the element particle — filtering at the palette was treating a symptom — and the naive reference matcher used by the property tests now encodes the same rule so the two oracles stay in step.
nodes.norm_label: differential harness finding: abstract substitution-group head accepted

nodes.label: Security model asserted rather than assumed
nodes.rationale: packages/xsd-libxml2/test/engine.test.ts feeds a billion-laughs bomb and an XXE payload pointing at file:///etc/passwd and checks that the first returns promptly instead of expanding and the second never yields the file's contents.
nodes.norm_label: security model asserted rather than assumed
nodes.community_name: Security model: client-side is not a security property

nodes.label: Three validators, one Diagnostic type
nodes.rationale: saxes for well-formedness during parse, libxml2 via WASM in a worker debounced ~150ms, and the fontoxpath Schematron interpreter — all emitting the same shape so the Problems panel, tree badges and explainer have exactly one thing to render. The guidance engine is an explicitly advisory fourth source.

nodes.label: XsdEngine interface
nodes.rationale: libxml2-wasm primary with xmllint-wasm as a named fallback behind one interface — same underlying C library, so switching is a driver swap rather than a rewrite. libxml2-wasm is preferred for its reusable compiled-schema handle, since xmlSchemaParse dominates cost in an interactive edit loop.

nodes.label: Explicit disposal of native-memory handles in the worker
nodes.rationale: A leak here is a wasm heap OOM, not a GC pause; ownership lives entirely in the worker, one handle per schema set, disposed on schema change.
nodes.norm_label: explicit disposal of native-memory handles in the worker

nodes.label: libxml2 demoted from authoritative validator to fast 1.0 oracle
nodes.rationale: libxml2 implements XML Schema 1.0 only and the maintainer has stated 1.1 is not planned; there is no JavaScript alternative, and Saxon-EE is a commercial per-seat Java product with no browser story.
nodes.norm_label: libxml2 demoted from authoritative validator to fast 1.0 oracle

nodes.label: XSD version detection prefers 1.1 when ambiguous
nodes.rationale: Detection comes from vc:minVersion/vc:maxVersion and from the presence of 1.1-only constructs; when ambiguous prefer 1.1 because it is the superset, and say which version was assumed.
nodes.norm_label: xsd version detection prefers 1.1 when ambiguous

nodes.label: Resolve the schema graph in JavaScript before calling into WASM
nodes.rationale: libxml2 will happily compile a schema with unresolved imports and then validate against the partial model, silently under-reporting errors — a correctness failure that looks like success. So walk the closure, resolve through the catalogue, rewrite to flat filenames, materialise into the WASM virtual FS, and assert the closure is complete.
nodes.norm_label: resolve the schema graph in javascript before calling into wasm
nodes.community_name: Security model: client-side is not a security property

nodes.label: ValidationPayload with lineMap
nodes.rationale: One element start-tag per line makes 'error at line 42' an O(1) exact lookup. This serialisation is only for validation and never written to disk, so it does not conflict with the lossless splice serializer. The rejected alternative — injecting tracking attributes — looks correct in a prototype and then fails against any strict schema with cvc-complex-type.3.2.2, because the injected attributes are themselves invalid.
nodes.community_name: Lossless CST document model, not the DOM

nodes.label: Revision tagging and terminate-and-respawn cancellation
nodes.rationale: A transparent proxy hides exactly the lifecycle control needed, which is why the protocol is hand-rolled rather than Comlink; in-flight results render dimmed rather than cleared so the UI never flickers through a misleading 'no problems' state mid-edit.

nodes.label: IDomFacade: our CST is the XPath data model
nodes.rationale: No second DOM, no sync problem, no serialisation round-trip.
nodes.norm_label: idomfacade: our cst is the xpath data model
nodes.community_name: Lossless CST document model, not the DOM

nodes.label: First-match-wins per context node
nodes.rationale: Within a pattern a node is claimed by the first rule whose context matches it and later rules do not fire. This is the semantic beginners trip over most, hence the shadowing detector.
nodes.community_name: whatCanGoHere: forward run intersected with backward co-reachability

nodes.label: @context is an XSLT match pattern, not an XPath expression
nodes.rationale: Prefixing descendant-or-self::node()/ unless it starts with / is correct for essentially all real-world contexts but diverges on predicates in certain positions; document the approximation and test it.
nodes.norm_label: @context is an xslt match pattern, not an xpath expression
nodes.community_name: whatCanGoHere: forward run intersected with backward co-reachability

nodes.label: queryBinding semantic drift
nodes.rationale: Running an xslt (XPath 1.0) schema under 3.1 keeps general comparisons existential but changes untyped string-vs-number comparisons, so warn on queryBinding="xslt".

nodes.label: Foreign XSLT in Schematron: detect and refuse explicitly
nodes.rationale: xsl:function, xsl:key, xsl:template and EXSLT cannot run on this interpreter, and some real healthcare and DITA Schematron uses them. Silently mis-validating is far worse than declining.
nodes.norm_label: foreign xslt in schematron: detect and refuse explicitly
nodes.community_name: whatCanGoHere: forward run intersected with backward co-reachability

nodes.label: Live rule testing — the killer beginner feature
nodes.rationale: Context match counts, per-rule fire counts, shadowing detection, per-assertion pass/fail lists and message preview with sch:value-of interpolated. It exists because the interpreter was chosen over the compiled pipeline, and it is what turns Schematron from an expert-only format into something a beginner can iterate on.
nodes.norm_label: live rule testing — the killer beginner feature
nodes.community_name: whatCanGoHere: forward run intersected with backward co-reachability

nodes.label: Compiled-expression cache and single-walk pattern evaluation
nodes.rationale: Naive evaluation is O(patterns x rules x nodes); mitigate with a cache keyed on (expression, namespaceBindings) using compileXPathToJavaScript, and evaluate patterns in one document walk rather than one traversal per rule.
nodes.norm_label: compiled-expression cache and single-walk pattern evaluation

nodes.label: The anti-drift differential harness
nodes.rationale: The guidance engine and the authoritative validators are independent implementations; disagreement means the product teaches beginners wrong things, which is worse than being merely buggy. Publish the pass rate — a number in CI output is the only thing that stops 'the engine works' from quietly becoming untrue.

nodes.label: SchXslt2 + xslt3 as the CI-only Schematron oracle
nodes.rationale: Never shipped to the browser; it targets ISO/IEC 19757-3:2025 and covers all but one feature of it, so our interpreter should target the same edition rather than the older 2016/2020 texts.
nodes.norm_label: schxslt2 + xslt3 as the ci-only schematron oracle

nodes.label: A .sch someone emailed you is executable code
nodes.rationale: Classical Schematron compiles to Turing-complete XSLT with fn:doc(), fn:unparsed-text() and xsl:result-document, so a malicious rule can exfiltrate the whole document with the user's network position and cookies — including Schematron embedded in xs:appinfo, which the user never consciously chose to run. The fontoxpath interpreter is safe by construction, a second independent justification for the interpreter decision.
nodes.norm_label: a .sch someone emailed you is executable code
nodes.community_name: whatCanGoHere: forward run intersected with backward co-reachability

nodes.label: If XSLT ever becomes necessary: null-origin sandboxed iframe
nodes.rationale: sandbox="allow-scripts" without allow-same-origin, under Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none', communicating by postMessage, with a Playwright test asserting zero network egress during validation.
nodes.norm_label: if xslt ever becomes necessary: null-origin sandboxed iframe
nodes.community_name: whatCanGoHere: forward run intersected with backward co-reachability

nodes.label: libxml2 parser flag policy
nodes.rationale: Always XML_PARSE_NONET; never NOENT, DTDLOAD, DTDATTR, XINCLUDE or HUGE. NOENT expands external entities and DTDLOAD fetches them, and libxml2's billion-laughs check is disabled by HUGE — exactly the flag someone turns on the first time a large document fails to parse.
nodes.community_name: Security model: client-side is not a security property

nodes.label: Never auto-fetch a remote schemaLocation
nodes.rationale: A named rule in the plan precisely because it is the most likely place someone adds a convenience fetch() six months in; the user sees the full URL and decides.
nodes.community_name: Security model: client-side is not a security property

nodes.label: One resolver, one choke point (src/io/resolver.ts)
nodes.rationale: Serves only buffers already in the in-app catalogue and every other URI returns not-found, which makes the no-fetch guarantee reviewable in one file rather than auditable across a codebase.
nodes.community_name: Security model: client-side is not a security property

nodes.label: No telemetry in v1
nodes.rationale: An enforceable promise because there is no server to send anything to; the optional CORS proxy fetches only schemas the user explicitly asked for and never sees document content.
nodes.community_name: Security model: client-side is not a security property

nodes.label: Four-region resizable layout
nodes.rationale: Sizes persisted per breakpoint bucket via react-resizable-panels autoSaveId; at 1280-1599 Source becomes a Ctrl+E overlay splitting the centre horizontally rather than stealing tree width; phone is explicitly out of scope rather than half-supported.
nodes.community_name: Inspector section stack and per-document-kind registry

nodes.label: Inspector section stack and per-document-kind registry
nodes.rationale: Everything about the selected node in one fixed place is the property beginners rely on most, and a registry lets XSD and Schematron swap sections in without a second layout implementation.
nodes.norm_label: inspector section stack and per-document-kind registry
nodes.community_name: Inspector section stack and per-document-kind registry

nodes.label: Tree row anatomy and density variables
nodes.rationale: Steal Chrome DevTools' Elements panel wholesale — badge chips, inline preview and a bottom breadcrumb are all proven at this density. The cardinality chip is literal ('2 of 0-∞') with tabular numerals so widths align, and indent guides for the focused node's ancestor chain are the cheapest orientation aid there is.
nodes.norm_label: tree row anatomy and density variables

nodes.label: Namespace colouring from eight curated OKLCH hues
nodes.rationale: Free hue rotation produces low-contrast near-duplicates, so hash into a curated set. Colour tints only the prefix chip background and the prefix text is always shown, so colour is decoration and never information (WCAG 1.4.1). Unprefixed elements get a neutral grey chip so beginners learn a namespace is still in play.
nodes.norm_label: namespace colouring from eight curated oklch hues

nodes.label: Pre-emptive drag and drop, never post-hoc revert
nodes.rationale: Blockly and Scratch established that refusing at the boundary teaches the rule, whereas snap-back after acceptance teaches nothing. The full legal-drop set is computed once at drag start by asking the content-model engine which (parent, index) pairs accept the dragged QName.
nodes.norm_label: pre-emptive drag and drop, never post-hoc revert
nodes.community_name: whatCanGoHere: forward run intersected with backward co-reachability

nodes.label: Filtering narrows rather than highlights
nodes.rationale: Non-matching nodes hide but every match's full ancestor chain stays visible at 60% opacity so it is obvious they are context rather than matches; Escape restores the previous expansion state exactly, which means storing it before filtering.

nodes.label: Insert palette specification
nodes.rationale: Groups in fixed order, never re-sorting as you type. Fuzzy search matches documentation text as well as element names so typing 'price' surfaces an element named amt. The preview pane is where teaching actually happens, and when nothing is legal the empty state explains why rather than showing an empty list.
nodes.community_name: whatCanGoHere: forward run intersected with backward co-reachability

nodes.label: 'Add all required' is recursive and fills values
nodes.rationale: Every generated value is marked a placeholder, counted in an app-bar chip, steppable with F7 and cleared on first user edit. This turns 'valid but meaningless' into a guided to-do list, which is exactly what a beginner needs after a wizard drops them into a filled skeleton.
nodes.norm_label: 'add all required' is recursive and fills values

nodes.label: Smart paste helper sheet
nodes.rationale: Each ranked option is annotated with its validity consequence and the highest-validity option is default-selected. Converts the single most error-prone beginner action into a teaching moment while staying one keystroke for experts.
nodes.community_name: whatCanGoHere: forward run intersected with backward co-reachability

nodes.label: Keyboard map — the contract
nodes.rationale: Follows the WAI-ARIA APG tree pattern; Escape must never trap focus inside the tree. Insert is bound four ways (Ctrl+Space for IDE muscle memory, / for Notion muscle memory, +, Insert).

nodes.label: src/schema/describe.ts — the documentation guarantee
nodes.rationale: Priority order is xs:documentation in the user's language, then an xs:appinfo label, then a generated sentence. Every palette row, tooltip and Form-view hint calls this one function so no code path can render a blank description.
nodes.community_name: whatCanGoHere: forward run intersected with backward co-reachability

nodes.label: 'Why is this invalid?' — a fixed four-section popover
nodes.rationale: Same popover, same four sections, same order from every error badge. The raw cvc-* message must be available for people who will paste it into a search engine but must never be the primary text.
nodes.norm_label: 'why is this invalid?' — a fixed four-section popover

nodes.label: cvc-catalogue.ts and svrl-catalogue.ts message templates
nodes.rationale: Every cvc-* code maps to a template with typed slots (found, expected[], path); RedHat lemminx's code-action set is the best ready-made list of fix actions to mirror.

nodes.label: Form view — same model, no second state tree
nodes.rationale: Do not introduce react-hook-form or a JSON-Schema form library: the XML model is the single source of truth and every control dispatches the same commands as the tree, or the project is spent reconciling two states. Mixed-content nodes are not form-renderable and say so rather than showing a broken form.
nodes.norm_label: form view — same model, no second state tree

nodes.label: Visible undo history panel
nodes.rationale: Labels are human sentences and clicking an entry time-travels and focuses affectedPath. Undo must always move focus and scroll to the affected node — silent undo is disorienting and is a top complaint about every editor in the prior art.
nodes.community_name: Lossless CST document model, not the DOM

nodes.label: Onboarding empty states and three bundled examples
nodes.rationale: Empty states carry their weight: an empty tree with a schema attached shows a single ghost row '+ Add root element' so the very first action is one click. The third example fails one Schematron rule on open so the user sees error to explainer to quick fix to green within the first 60 seconds.
nodes.norm_label: onboarding empty states and three bundled examples

nodes.label: New-document wizard — five steps
nodes.rationale: Every step is back-navigable and the whole wizard is escapable to a blank-with-schema state. Never trap a user in a wizard they opened by accident. The optional step 4 collects top-level required values so the document is not born full of placeholders.

nodes.label: Expert mode differences table
nodes.rationale: Nothing is removed in either direction — an expert can still open the explainer, a beginner can still reach the raw source.

nodes.label: role="tree" with aria-activedescendant, rejecting treegrid
nodes.rationale: Treegrid's screen-reader support is inconsistent with dynamically-inserted rows and our rows have a variable number of cells, which breaks the grid's column model. activedescendant is forced by virtualization, which unmounts rows and would destroy DOM focus; VoiceOver handles it less well, compensated by an explicit polite live region.

nodes.label: One debounced polite live region and the delta-only rule
nodes.rationale: Validation announces the delta only, never the absolute count on every keystroke; one announce() helper debounced to at most one announcement per 1500ms so the region does not become noise, with role="alert" reserved for save-blocking errors.
nodes.norm_label: one debounced polite live region and the delta-only rule

nodes.label: Visual design tokens
nodes.rationale: Radix Colors 12-step OKLCH primitives behind semantic aliases, with dark mode using matching scales under identical alias names. Do not height-animate tree expand/collapse — animate only the twisty rotation, because height animation on a virtualized list janks badly. Nine custom glyphs cover XML semantics Lucide lacks.

nodes.label: XSD authoring mode UI
nodes.rationale: minOccurs/maxOccurs render as one editable 0..∞ control rather than two attributes buried in a list; the documentation card is editable because writing xs:documentation is the highest-leverage thing an XSD author can do for downstream users of this very editor. The Diagram tab is deferred since beginners cannot read that notation anyway.

nodes.label: Schematron authoring mode UI
nodes.rationale: The document is shallow so the Inspector swaps its attributes-first layout for a CodeMirror 6 XPath editor with namespace-aware completion from sch:ns. Pleasing reuse: Schematron is itself defined by a schema, so the same content-model engine drives this palette with no special-casing.
nodes.community_name: whatCanGoHere: forward run intersected with backward co-reachability

nodes.label: Prior art — steal precisely, and what to avoid
nodes.rationale: XMLSpy's Grid View table collapse, XXE's insert model, Oxygen's content-completion side pane, lemminx's code-action catalogue verbatim, nxml-mode's continuous validation. Avoided: Oxygen's mode dichotomy (users get stranded in a mode that cannot do what they want), XMLSpy's three stacked unexplained entry-helper panes (the anti-pattern this product exists to fix), and surfacing raw cvc-* strings as primary text.
nodes.norm_label: prior art — steal precisely, and what to avoid

nodes.label: Virtualization forces three design consequences
nodes.rationale: Fixed-height rows per density (so inline previews truncate rather than wrap), aria-activedescendant rather than DOM focus, and a guarded 'Expand all'. Plus: debounce selection-to-inspector at 60ms or held arrow keys stutter, and memoise palette candidates per (parent type, position) or they recompute on every filter keystroke.

nodes.label: The lossless contract: identical bytes, not semantically equivalent
nodes.rationale: Users keep these files in git and a tool that reformats on save produces a four-thousand-line diff on every commit. Everything above this package assumes it can edit a document without damaging the parts nobody touched.
nodes.norm_label: the lossless contract: identical bytes, not semantically equivalent
nodes.community_name: Lossless CST document model, not the DOM

nodes.label: Exact byte spans: every byte belongs to exactly one token
nodes.rationale: An untouched node is re-emitted by slicing the original source and only dirty nodes are regenerated, which makes fidelity structural rather than a matter of reproducing a hundred formatting details, and makes serialization O(changed) rather than O(document).
nodes.norm_label: exact byte spans: every byte belongs to exactly one token
nodes.community_name: Lossless CST document model, not the DOM

nodes.label: The tokenizer does not decide validity
nodes.rationale: It recovers, because a beginner's document is malformed most of the time it is being edited and refusing to open a broken file is a product failure.
nodes.norm_label: the tokenizer does not decide validity

nodes.label: wellformed.ts — an independent saxes-based validity oracle
nodes.rationale: A second implementation, so a tokenizer bug cannot quietly make a broken document look fine; the two are diffed against each other in the tests.
nodes.norm_label: wellformed.ts — an independent saxes-based validity oracle

nodes.label: Mutation through commands that carry their own inverse
nodes.rationale: Undo is exact rather than a re-parse, node ids stay stable across history navigation so selection and diagnostics survive, and every command carries a human label — which is what makes a visible History panel possible later.
nodes.norm_label: mutation through commands that carry their own inverse
nodes.community_name: Lossless CST document model, not the DOM

nodes.label: Property-based round-trip and apply-invert identity tests
nodes.rationale: Arbitrary generated documents round-trip byte-for-byte (500 runs) and apply-then-invert is the identity over random command sequences (300 runs) — an undo model that is subtly non-inverting corrupts documents in ways users only notice much later.
nodes.norm_label: property-based round-trip and apply-invert identity tests
nodes.community_name: Lossless CST document model, not the DOM

nodes.label: Install the differential oracles step (xmlschema, lxml)
nodes.rationale: Without them our engine would be the only implementation of XSD 1.1 and of Schematron in the stack, with nothing checking it — PLAN.md §11 risk 2 exactly. Both are pure-Python installs so there is nothing to build.
nodes.norm_label: install the differential oracles step (xmlschema, lxml)

nodes.label: Check the bundle budget step (scripts/check-bundle.mjs)
nodes.rationale: A stray top-level import pulling a validator into the main chunk is a one-line mistake that costs every user the download and looks like nothing. It has happened once already, so it is checked rather than remembered.

nodes.label: pnpm/action-setup without an explicit version
nodes.rationale: pnpm/action-setup errors if the version is given both in the action config and in package.json's packageManager field; package.json wins.

nodes.label: CI concurrency group with cancel-in-progress
nodes.rationale: A branch with an open PR would otherwise run twice per push, once for each trigger.

nodes.label: Deploy to GitHub Pages workflow
nodes.rationale: Least-privilege permissions (contents read, pages write, id-token write) and a pages concurrency group that never cancels a running deployment but queues behind it.

nodes.label: BASE_PATH build env for the project Pages site
nodes.rationale: A project Pages site is served from /<repo>/, so the base path must match the repo name.
nodes.norm_label: base_path build env for the project pages site

nodes.label: SPA fallback: copy index.html to 404.html
nodes.rationale: Pages has no rewrite rules, so a 404 copy of index.html is how a client-routed app survives a deep link or a refresh.

nodes.label: PWA manifest and theme-color links
nodes.community_name: Security model: client-side is not a security property

nodes.label: Rounded Square Badge (32x32, rx=7, blue fill)
nodes.norm_label: rounded square badge (32x32, rx=7, blue fill)
nodes.community_name: Editor App Favicon (32x32 SVG app icon)

nodes.label: Outward Angle Bracket Glyph (white chevron pair)
nodes.norm_label: outward angle bracket glyph (white chevron pair)
nodes.community_name: Editor App Favicon (32x32 SVG app icon)

nodes.label: Brand Blue #2563eb
nodes.rationale: #2563eb is Tailwind's blue-600, the framework default primary. Using the palette token verbatim rather than a bespoke hex keeps the icon in lockstep with in-app accent colours without a shared design-token pipeline.
nodes.community_name: Editor App Favicon (32x32 SVG app icon)

nodes.label: Code Editor Visual Identity (brackets as product signifier)
nodes.rationale: The mark is a pair of outward-facing angle brackets rather than a wordmark or letterform. Brackets are the near-universal shorthand for source code, so the icon reads as a code/text editor at a glance and stays legible in a browser tab where no accompanying label is visible. It also avoids tying the icon to a product name, so renaming the app does not invalidate the asset.
nodes.norm_label: code editor visual identity (brackets as product signifier)
nodes.community_name: Editor App Favicon (32x32 SVG app icon)

nodes.label: Scalable Vector Favicon Strategy
nodes.rationale: Shipping a single SVG instead of a multi-resolution .ico or a set of PNGs: one ~300-byte file renders crisply at every density and OS icon size, needs no build step or raster pipeline, and can be served straight from the static public/ directory. Trade-off is no support in very old browsers, which is acceptable for a modern web editor.
nodes.community_name: Editor App Favicon (32x32 SVG app icon)

nodes.label: Small-Size Legibility Constraints (heavy stroke, round caps, max contrast)
nodes.rationale: Every drawing choice is tuned for a 16px tab render: stroke-width 2.6 on a 32-unit canvas (~8% of width) survives downscaling where a hairline would vanish; pure white on saturated blue maximises contrast; round line caps and joins prevent mitre spikes from aliasing into noise; fill=none keeps the mark an open figure so the two brackets stay separable.
nodes.norm_label: small-size legibility constraints (heavy stroke, round caps, max contrast)
nodes.community_name: Editor App Favicon (32x32 SVG app icon)

nodes.label: Static public/ Asset Convention
nodes.rationale: Living under apps/editor/public/ means the file is copied verbatim to the web root by the bundler and referenced by an absolute /favicon.svg URL from the app's HTML shell, bypassing module hashing so the path stays stable across builds.
nodes.community_name: Editor App Favicon (32x32 SVG app icon)
